title: Build an Engaged Social Media Audience
description: Grow followers by 25% and reach an average engagement rate of 4% within 60 days by posting 5 times per week across our main platforms. The team will plan a content calendar, write platform-specific captions, and review top-performing posts weekly to improve results.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Confirm which accounts are Zedu's and record a baseline first, then run the five-a-week calendar
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Growth of 25% needs a starting number, and today the accounts themselves are unclear: on 22 Oct 2026 every zedu.chat footer links to instagram.com/telex.im, tiktok.com/@telexim and x.com/teleximapp, plus a Facebook profile by numeric ID, so posting before that's settled grows the old brand. Plan: 1) with the team, confirm the official account on each platform (renaming the Telex handles is a separate goal) and record today's followers and the last 30 days' engagement rate per platform; 2) pick the two main platforms where cohort operators are (likely LinkedIn and X) and plan five posts a week built from problems operators post about publicly, each tied to one real feature; 3) review the top posts weekly against the baseline and adjust. Tasks: account and baseline audit (research), 4-week calendar with captions (content), weekly review template (other).

A 25% follower-growth target needs a starting number, and the idea spots that every zedu.chat footer still links to the old Telex handles. Confirming the real accounts and recording a baseline first stops us growing the wrong brand, and makes the 25% and 4% targets measurable.

This puts account ownership and a real follower/engagement baseline before the growth target, and the live footer currently points social visitors to Telex-branded accounts. Confirming the right handles first avoids spending content effort on accounts that may not represent Zedu.

The goal sets a measurable target (25% follower growth, 4% engagement) and today neither number can be measured or moved, because every zedu.chat footer link still points at the old Telex accounts. Confirming which accounts are Zedu's and recording today's follower and engagement numbers turns 'grow by 25%' into something a weekly review can actually check, and it stops the team spending a 60-day window posting into accounts that are not Zedu's. That is a prerequisite rather than a detour, and it splits cleanly into three finishable tasks (account and baseline audit, calendar with captions, weekly review template).

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Educator story-led content engine with a weekly review loop
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Run the account as a repeatable engine, not ad-hoc posts. Three content pillars drawn from what educators actually struggle with: cohort management tips, one live Zedu feature tip per week, and real educator stories. Captions written platform-specific, posts batched weekly so five posts a week never slip, and a fixed weekly review of top performers to double down on what earns engagement. Every post ties to a live Zedu feature or a real use case, so the account grows by being useful. Measurement from week one: followers, per-post engagement rate, and profile visits, reviewed against the 25% follower and 4% engagement targets every Friday.

upvotes.reason: "Educator story-led content engine with a weekly review loop" is a specific deliverable for this goal with a way to check it was done properly. it fills a gap the goal has open rather than restating what is already covered.

upvotes.reason: Specific and deliverable: three content pillars with a named weekly cadence (five posts a week), platform-specific captions, and a fixed weekly review of top performers against stated targets. The measurement plan (followers, per-post engagement rate, profile visits) is concrete.

The three content themes, weekly batch cadence and performance review give this audience-growth goal a repeatable plan, while followers, engagement and profile visits track the stated targets. It complements the accepted workstream that first confirms official accounts and sets a baseline.

Three pillars drawn from what educators actually struggle with, plus one live feature tip a week, is a schedule a person can keep running, and batching weekly is what stops week four going quiet. Two things make this better than a posting list: every post must tie to a live Zedu feature or a real use case, which is what keeps the claims honest without a second review pass, and the fixed weekly review of top performers turns the calendar into something that improves on evidence instead of habit. The 25% follower and 4% engagement targets give the review a line to measure against from week one.

Every week five posts must exist somewhere; a fixed pillar + batch + review loop is the only structure here that makes the goal's 5-posts-a-week cadence survivable, and tying each post to a live feature is exactly the engagement goal says it wants.

downvotes.reason: Two sentences with no deliverables, tasks or named keyword source. It does not say how keyword research changes the five posts a week or the engagement and follower targets.

The keyword research is the smallest part of this job and the idea names no keyword source, no task, and no measure of how search demand changes the five weekly posts or the 25% follower and 4% engagement targets. A calendar is also already the second half of the other approach in this goal, so approving both would create two overlapping posting plans and still leave the team with no baseline and no confirmed accounts. The keyword input is worth keeping, but it belongs folded into a plan that starts with the accounts and the baseline rather than standing as its own approach.

downvotes.reason: Profile bio and search optimisation is a small one-off tweak, not a plan for 5 posts a week, and it gives no way to move the 25 percent follower or 4 percent engagement targets. No steps or tasks.

Searching for a brand's profile bio is a small part of how people find a social account, and the idea has no tasks, numbers or baseline. It also ignores that the footer links still point to the old Telex handles. A profile clean-up only helps after the real accounts are confirmed. I would fold it into the baseline-first approach.

A profile bio and description clean-up is a one-off tweak that cannot move 25% follower growth or 4% engagement, and it cannot even be applied to the right accounts yet, since every zedu.chat footer link still points at the old Telex handles rather than Zedu's own. There are no tasks and no way to check whether it worked. Once the official accounts and the baseline are confirmed, tightening the bios is a sensible item to fold into the calendar work in this goal, but on its own it is not an approach to growing an audience.

downvotes.reason: Building SEO landing pages is website work, not the social audience-growth work the goal asks for, and the idea gives no pages, steps or measure. It drifts off the goal.

The goal is 25% follower growth and 4% engagement from five posts a week. This idea builds landing pages, which is a separate web project that does not move either number. It has no evidence that social visitors need dedicated pages and no tasks to check. A posting plan with a baseline serves the goal more directly.

This builds website pages, which is a different kind of work from what this goal measures, and Zedu already has solution pages for bootcamps and schools, so it repeats work that other goals in this project already own rather than adding a new search surface. It also does nothing for either number the goal is judged on: follower growth and engagement rate from posting five times a week. A posting plan with a recorded baseline and a weekly review against it is what actually moves those two numbers.
